card.summary: Text→video on HunyuanVideo 1.5 at 720p fp16 (24 GB). The text→video counterpart to the 1.5 image→video editor; real CFG with negative prompts.
card.pick_when: You want a 720p text→video clip with HunyuanVideo 1.5 quality on a 24 GB card.

prompt.guidance: Describe the motion/scene; the prompt directs the motion.
prompt.example: a lantern-lit night market in the rain, neon reflections on wet stone, slow dolly forward, cinematic
prompt.overview: Describe the whole scene from scratch following the official formula: Subject + Motion + Scene + [Shot Type] + [Camera Movement] + [Lighting] + [Style] + [Atmosphere].
prompt.instructions: HunyuanVideo 1.5 (Qwen2.5-VL + ByT5 encoders) is built around the official T2V formula 'Subject + Motion + Scene + [Shot] + [Camera] + [Lighting] + [Style] + [Atmosphere]', using concise, direct vocabulary (bracketed layers are optional). Tencent says longer, detailed prompts measurably improve output; sequence actions in temporal order with connectives ('first... then... meanwhile... finally...') and use concrete actions and spatial references instead of abstract emotion words. Wrap any in-frame text in quotation marks (ByT5 glyph encoder). Built-in prompt rewriting auto-expands short prompts, but the formula works directly.
do: Follow the T2V formula: Subject + Motion + Scene + optional Shot/Camera/Lighting/Style/Atmosphere
Sequence actions temporally with connectives: 'first... then... meanwhile... finally...'
Use concrete observable actions and spatial references (left/right frame, foreground/background)
Use standard camera-move terms: dolly, pan, tilt, orbit, tracking, crane, fixed/static
Wrap on-screen text in quotation marks for accurate text rendering
Use a single clear shot intent and a coherent action sequence
dont: Don't rely on vague emotional language without concrete action/visual cues
Don't assume you must run an external rewriter - the formula works directly
Don't lean on negative prompts to fix quality on distilled checkpoints
Don't over-stuff contradictory camera moves or styles in one clip
Don't omit the subject/scene (t2v invents everything from text)
examples: A tired middle-aged Asian man in a pilling grey sweater, fine wrinkles around his eyes, looks out the window with a worried expression; he slowly exhales and lowers his gaze. Fixed camera, cinematic lighting, photorealism style, tense and melancholic atmosphere.
prompt.negative_guidance: Negatives are supported (default empty) and apply only to standard checkpoints at the recommended CFG~6; on cfg-distilled variants (guidance_scale=1) they have little effect. The non-distilled real-CFG t2v variant responds to negatives.
